papers.title: A Sensor-Integrated, Explainable Machine-Learning Digital-Twin Framework for Field-Validated Service-Life Prediction of Cementitious Materials under Coupled Chloride–Sulfate Carbonation Degradation
papers.abstract: Abstract Reinforced cementitious infrastructure is subjected to all of these mechanisms – chloride ingress, sulfate attack, carbonation, and freeze-thaw or alkali silica cycling – during its service life, but most of the available service-life models treat these mechanisms separately. There are a number of coupled mechanisms that are not currently covered by the industry standard approaches such as classical deterministic Fick’s second law, or semi-probabilistic approaches such as Life-365, DuraCrete and the fib Model Code for Service Life Design, for which it is not yet possible to find broadly accepted models. At the same time, a large number of machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) studies have developed to be able to predict short-term performance with higher accuracy, but as recently summarized in the RILEM Technical Committee 315-DCS and related reviews, most of the studies are based on laboratory generated data, with only limited field validation, few open datasets and very poor model interpretability. After synthesising available evidence on degradation mechanisms, microstructural characterisation, supplementary cementitious materials, self-healing technologies, classical service-life models, and ML/digital-twin structural health monitoring, the present authors conclude that a specific research gap, identified in the literature, lies in the absence of an explainable, sensor-integrated, digital-twin framework that couples multi-hazard mechanistic degradation models with field-updatable machine learning for cementitious materials. This updated version clearly aligns the proposed contribution with six more recent digital-twin and ML-durability frameworks (Section 3.1); develops the governing mathematical formulations for each layer (Section 5); develops a computational workflow and synchronisation algorithm (Section 5.1); expands the explainable-AI and machine-learning methodology (Sections 5.5–5.6); adds a practical implementation and uncertainty-propagation treatment (Section 5.7 and Section 8). A five-layer conceptual framework is suggested that merges embedded electrochemical and optical sensing with a coupled chloride-sulfate-carbonation reactive-transport core, a physics-informed explainable ML layer, Bayesian updating of the digital twin, and a decision support output that is interpretable. A validation strategy, based on existing accelerated-exposure and field-monitoring datasets, is outlined and the framework is illustrated with literature-derived parameter ranges. The paper is written in a concept and method-oriented manner and not to report new laboratory results.

papers.title: Surface Finishing Of PBF-LB Stainless Steels Using Chemical And Chemical-Mechanical Polishing In Combination With Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) For Improved Mechanical Performance
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the production of metal components with complex geometries; however, surface and near-surface defects inherent to powder-based processing limit mechanical performance and component qualification. Surface-related features, such as partially fused particles and near-surface porosity, significantly reduce fatigue life, thereby restricting adoption in high-reliability applications. Improving surface quality through chemical polishing (CP) and chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) provides a viable pathway to enhance structural reliability. This study evaluates CP and CMP in combination with hot isostatic pressing (HIP) as strategies to mitigate surface and subsurface defects in PBF-LB\17-4 PH, 15-5 PH, and 316L. The influence of surface roughness and microstructural evolution on tensile properties and high-cycle fatigue performance was examined. Results demonstrate clear process–structure–property relationships linking powder-derived surface condition, post-processing strategy, and mechanical performance. These findings support robust, qualification-ready post-processing routes for AM stainless steel components. This work was supported by the USAF-SBIR Program under Contract FA864923P1086.
papers.summary: 粉末增材制造能够成形复杂金属构件，但表面与近表面缺陷会限制疲劳寿命和构件鉴定。本研究评估化学抛光、化学机械抛光与热等静压联合处理三类不锈钢，考察表面粗糙度及微观组织演变与拉伸性能、高周疲劳表现的关系。摘要称结果建立了清晰的工艺—组织—性能关联，但未报告具体改善幅度、试验参数或统计证据。本文适合作为增材制造构件疲劳可靠性后处理研究的线索，当前仅作摘要级解读。[摘要]

raw_metadata.title_zh: 化学及化学机械抛光联合热等静压改善激光粉末床熔融不锈钢的力学性能

article.lead: 粉末床熔融激光束（PBF-LB）不锈钢的表面与近表面缺陷可能限制疲劳表现和构件资格认定。本文关注化学抛光、化学机械抛光与热等静压组合处理，为理解后处理与力学性能的联系提供线索。

sections.title: 表面缺陷为何牵动疲劳可靠性
paragraphs: 增材制造能够制造复杂几何形状的金属构件，但粉末加工带来的表面及近表面缺陷会限制力学性能与构件资格认定。摘要特别提到未完全熔合颗粒和近表面孔隙，并指出这类表面特征会显著降低疲劳寿命，进而制约其在高可靠性应用中的采用。
改善表面质量被视为提升结构可靠性的可行途径。本文聚焦PBF-LB制造的17-4 PH、15-5 PH和316L不锈钢，考察化学抛光（CP）、化学机械抛光（CMP）与热等静压（HIP）的组合策略。

sections.title: 围绕后处理、组织与性能展开考察
paragraphs: 摘要说明，研究评估CP和CMP结合HIP，以减轻表面及亚表面缺陷；同时考察表面粗糙度和微观组织演变对拉伸性能与高周疲劳表现的影响。其研究框架将粉末加工形成的表面状态、后处理策略与力学表现联系起来。
摘要没有给出具体抛光或HIP参数，也没有展开试样制备、测试流程等细节，因此本文解读仅限于其明确列出的处理类别与考察指标。

sections.title: 摘要报告工艺—组织—性能联系
paragraphs: 作者报告了清晰的工艺—组织—性能关系，连接粉末加工形成的表面状态、后处理策略和力学性能。摘要据此认为，这些发现支持为增材制造不锈钢构件制定稳健、面向资格认定的后处理路线。
不过，摘要没有列出具体粗糙度、拉伸或疲劳结果，也未说明不同材料或处理组合的效果方向与幅度。因而这里能确认的是作者报告了上述关系及其应用指向，不能据此推定某种处理带来多大性能提升。

paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断样本安排、具体比较条件、统计处理及验证范围；这些内容是否在论文其他部分交代，也不能由摘要确定。摘要虽提及三种不锈钢和多项性能考察，但未提供足以比较各材料、处理组合或应用场景的细节。

article.lead: 粉末床熔融激光束（PBF-LB）不锈钢的表面与近表面缺陷可能限制疲劳表现和构件资格认定。本文关注化学抛光、化学机械抛光与热等静压组合处理，为理解后处理与力学性能的联系提供线索。

sections.title: 表面缺陷为何牵动疲劳可靠性
paragraphs: 增材制造能够制造复杂几何形状的金属构件，但粉末加工带来的表面及近表面缺陷会限制力学性能与构件资格认定。摘要特别提到未完全熔合颗粒和近表面孔隙，并指出这类表面特征会显著降低疲劳寿命，进而制约其在高可靠性应用中的采用。
改善表面质量被视为提升结构可靠性的可行途径。本文聚焦PBF-LB制造的17-4 PH、15-5 PH和316L不锈钢，考察化学抛光（CP）、化学机械抛光（CMP）与热等静压（HIP）的组合策略。

sections.title: 围绕后处理、组织与性能展开考察
paragraphs: 摘要说明，研究评估CP和CMP结合HIP，以减轻表面及亚表面缺陷；同时考察表面粗糙度和微观组织演变对拉伸性能与高周疲劳表现的影响。其研究框架将粉末加工形成的表面状态、后处理策略与力学表现联系起来。
摘要没有给出具体抛光或HIP参数，也没有展开试样制备、测试流程等细节，因此本文解读仅限于其明确列出的处理类别与考察指标。

sections.title: 摘要报告工艺—组织—性能联系
paragraphs: 作者报告了清晰的工艺—组织—性能关系，连接粉末加工形成的表面状态、后处理策略和力学性能。摘要据此认为，这些发现支持为增材制造不锈钢构件制定稳健、面向资格认定的后处理路线。
不过，摘要没有列出具体粗糙度、拉伸或疲劳结果，也未说明不同材料或处理组合的效果方向与幅度。因而这里能确认的是作者报告了上述关系及其应用指向，不能据此推定某种处理带来多大性能提升。

sections.title: 摘要能支持的判断边界
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断样本安排、具体比较条件、统计处理及验证范围；这些内容是否在论文其他部分交代，也不能由摘要确定。摘要虽提及三种不锈钢和多项性能考察，但未提供足以比较各材料、处理组合或应用场景的细节。

sections.title: 阅读启发：追问关系如何落到资格认定
paragraphs: 阅读启发：进一步阅读全文时，可关注作者如何呈现表面状态、微观组织与拉伸及高周疲劳表现之间的证据，以及不同不锈钢和后处理组合的比较边界。摘要提出面向资格认定的应用指向，但具体依据与适用范围仍需结合论文正文判断。

papers.title: Seamless Deployment of Machine Learning Inference at the Far Edge: An Empirical AWS IoT Greengrass Architecture for Industrial Predictive Maintenance
papers.abstract: Industrial IoT sensors produce continuous, high-volume data streams that predictive maintenance needs to analyse in real time. Cloud-centric architectures send all raw telemetry to central servers, which costs latency, bandwidth and resilience. This paper presents a hybrid cloud-edge architecture for manufacturing predictive maintenance built on AWS IoT Core and AWS IoT Greengrass v2, with local machine learning inference at the edge and selective cloud synchronization. We deploy two configurations on real AWS infrastructure and compare them: a cloud-only baseline (Configuration A) and the proposed hybrid edge architecture (Configuration B). We measure end-to-end inference latency, bandwidth consumption and inference accuracy. Configuration B cuts cloud-bound bandwidth by 86.8% (63.6 KB to 7.2 KB per 200-reading window) and decision latency by 256x (23.1 ms cloud round trip to 0.09 ms local inference). At the edge, with no cloud involvement, it keeps an anomaly-class F1 score of 0.84 and 91% recall. The evaluation also instruments system uptime and Stream Manager queuing under cloud disconnection; the quantitative disconnection experiment is left as planned work. Our review of the literature points to four gaps that this work addresses: the lack of empirically validated Greengrass v2 deployments for predictive maintenance, unquantified bandwidth savings from selective edge synchronization, unmeasured resilience under cloud disconnection, and the open MLOps feedback loop at the edge.

papers.title: Scientific Machine Learning-Based Climate-Adaptive Co-Design of Electric Bus Charging Infrastructure and Control
papers.abstract: Electric bus operators must limit charging-infrastructure investment while supplying enough layover energy to preserve battery reserves during service. Climate changes both energy demand and charging acceptance, linking forecasts to control and infrastructure selection. We propose a scientific machine learning (SciML) framework for climate-adaptive co-design that predicts bus energy from an equipment-based physical prior and multimodal residual learning. Day-level calibration converts forecasts into upper energies that determine inventory targets and charging-window commitments; linear-programming screening is followed by closed-loop qualification of site sets. Public weather and reconstructed Montréal and Singapore duties drive continuous-year simulation with one vehicle configuration. With 28 target fitting days plus 40 calibration days, Singapore-to-Montréal transfer lowers 2025 forecast error by 5.4% against full fine-tuning and 18.7% against gradient boosting. Removing the physical prior and route-network inputs raises error 2.3 to 3.0 times. In 2025, reverse transfer lowers error by 58.0% against the calibrated physical prior and remains 11.3% above gradient boosting. Prediction accuracy and reserve outcomes rank the frozen predictors differently. On Singapore's eight-site design under fixed control in 2025, gradient boosting has the lowest forecast error but 135.03 lost days per operating seed, compared with 9.80 for transfer and 0.43 for the calibrated physical prior. Lost days count failures beyond a forecast-free full-site Reference plus uncommitted dates. Predictor-specific control pairing lowers transfer's lost days from 9.80 to 0.30. In Montréal, qualification restores the terminal needed on the coldest development day. The qualified eight-site predictive design lowers annual charging-subsystem cost by 28.2% against the full-site Reference.
papers.summary: 本文研究气候影响下电动公交充电设施投资与运营电量保障的协同设计。作者结合设备物理先验与多模态残差学习预测能耗，通过逐日校准、线性规划筛选和闭环验证选择站点及控制方案。摘要报告，预测误差最低的模型并不一定带来最少的运营失效，匹配预测器的控制可显著改善结果。合格的八站点方案相对全站点参考降低年度充电子系统成本28.2%。证据来自重构任务的连续全年仿真，不能视为实地验证。[摘要]

raw_metadata.title_zh: 基于科学机器学习的气候自适应电动公交充电基础设施与控制协同设计

article.lead: 电动公交如何少建充电设施，又不牺牲运营中的电池储备？这项研究将气候相关能耗预测、充电控制与站点选择联合设计，提醒读者：**预测更准，不一定意味着运营更可靠。**

sections.title: 气候同时改变耗电需求与充电能力
paragraphs: 公交运营方既要控制充电基础设施投资，又必须利用停站时间补足能量，维持服务期间的电池储备。气候不仅影响车辆能量需求，也影响充电接受能力，因此，预测模型不能脱离充电控制和基础设施选择单独评价。

sections.title: 从物理先验预测走向站点闭环检验
paragraphs: 作者提出科学机器学习（SciML）框架，以基于设备的物理先验结合多模态残差学习预测公交能耗，再通过日级校准形成能量上界，确定能量库存目标和充电时间窗承诺。站点集合先经线性规划筛选，再接受闭环资格检验。
研究使用公开天气数据与重建的蒙特利尔、新加坡运营任务，在一种车辆配置下开展连续全年仿真。因此，摘要报告的是仿真评价，而非已完成的实车部署验证。

sections.title: 误差排名与储备表现出现分离
paragraphs: 使用28个目标域拟合日及40个校准日，从新加坡向蒙特利尔迁移时，2025年预测误差较全量微调降低5.4%，较梯度提升降低18.7%。移除物理先验与线路网络输入后，误差增至2.3至3.0倍。反向迁移则较校准后的物理先验降低58.0%，但仍比梯度提升高11.3%，说明迁移收益具有方向差异。
在新加坡2025年的八站点设计及固定控制下，梯度提升预测误差最低，但每个运营随机种子的损失天数为135.03；迁移模型和校准后的物理先验分别为9.80和0.43。该指标统计相对于不依赖预测的全站点参考方案额外发生的失败，并计入未承诺日期，不能直接等同于实际停运天数。
为预测器配对相应控制后，迁移模型的损失天数由9.80降至0.30。在蒙特利尔，资格检验恢复了开发阶段最冷日所需的终点站。通过资格检验的八站点预测型设计，相比全站点参考方案降低年度充电子系统成本28.2%；这一结果不等于公交系统总成本下降。

sections.title: 单一车辆配置下的结果，边界仍需细读
paragraphs: 摘要明确给出了拟合与校准天数，但未交代完整数据规模、运营随机种子数量、误差指标定义及不确定性范围。现有信息也不足以判断不同控制配对的比较条件，以及结论对其他车辆、城市和实际运营的适用性。这些属于摘要无法判断的内容，不能据此断言论文未开展相关分析。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把预测放回控制与成本中评价
paragraphs: 阅读启发：面向智能运维与可靠性优化，值得追问的不是哪个预测器误差最小，而是它如何经过校准、控制配对与站点检验转化为储备保障。进一步阅读可重点关注损失天数的定义、控制配对规则，以及成本节约对应的可靠性约束，而不宜仅凭预测精度选择方案。

article.lead: 电动公交如何少建充电设施，又不牺牲运营中的电池储备？这项研究将气候相关能耗预测、充电控制与站点选择联合设计，提醒读者：**预测更准，不一定意味着运营更可靠。**

sections.title: 气候同时改变耗电需求与充电能力
paragraphs: 公交运营方既要控制充电基础设施投资，又必须利用停站时间补足能量，维持服务期间的电池储备。气候不仅影响车辆能量需求，也影响充电接受能力，因此，预测模型不能脱离充电控制和基础设施选择单独评价。

sections.title: 从物理先验预测走向站点闭环检验
paragraphs: 作者提出科学机器学习（SciML）框架，以基于设备的物理先验结合多模态残差学习预测公交能耗，再通过日级校准形成能量上界，确定能量库存目标和充电时间窗承诺。站点集合先经线性规划筛选，再接受闭环资格检验。
研究使用公开天气数据与重建的蒙特利尔、新加坡运营任务，在一种车辆配置下开展连续全年仿真。因此，摘要报告的是仿真评价，而非已完成的实车部署验证。

sections.title: 误差排名与储备表现出现分离
paragraphs: 使用28个目标域拟合日及40个校准日，从新加坡向蒙特利尔迁移时，2025年预测误差较全量微调降低5.4%，较梯度提升降低18.7%。移除物理先验与线路网络输入后，误差增至2.3至3.0倍。反向迁移则较校准后的物理先验降低58.0%，但仍比梯度提升高11.3%，说明迁移收益具有方向差异。
在新加坡2025年的八站点设计及固定控制下，梯度提升预测误差最低，但每个运营随机种子的损失天数为135.03；迁移模型和校准后的物理先验分别为9.80和0.43。该指标统计相对于不依赖预测的全站点参考方案额外发生的失败，并计入未承诺日期，不能直接等同于实际停运天数。
为预测器配对相应控制后，迁移模型的损失天数由9.80降至0.30。在蒙特利尔，资格检验恢复了开发阶段最冷日所需的终点站。通过资格检验的八站点预测型设计，相比全站点参考方案降低年度充电子系统成本28.2%；这一结果不等于公交系统总成本下降。

sections.title: 单一车辆配置下的结果，边界仍需细读
paragraphs: 摘要明确给出了拟合与校准天数，但未交代完整数据规模、运营随机种子数量、误差指标定义及不确定性范围。现有信息也不足以判断不同控制配对的比较条件，以及结论对其他车辆、城市和实际运营的适用性。这些属于摘要无法判断的内容，不能据此断言论文未开展相关分析。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把预测放回控制与成本中评价
paragraphs: 阅读启发：面向智能运维与可靠性优化，值得追问的不是哪个预测器误差最小，而是它如何经过校准、控制配对与站点检验转化为储备保障。进一步阅读可重点关注损失天数的定义、控制配对规则，以及成本节约对应的可靠性约束，而不宜仅凭预测精度选择方案。

papers.title: Beyond global drug-likeness: The FamDLike framework as a target family-specific drug-likeness score.
papers.abstract: Drug-likeness is a central metric which is used to evaluate the physicochemical profile of small molecules either as a filter for virtual screening or, more recently, as a reward function in generative design tasks. Established scores such as QED are widely adopted for these purposes, although the ligands of different therapeutic target families occupy different regions of physicochemical space. Applying a single global drug-likeness criterion can therefore systematically reward some target classes while penalising others, narrowing the chemical space considered druglike in a way that may not reflect the actual requirements for a given project. In this work, we propose a target family specific drug-likeness approach, the FamDLike framework, designed to distinguish target families more accurately than existing metrics and to explore family specific druglike regions of chemical space. This framework combines three complementary modelling paradigms: desirability functions, generalized additive models and tree-based machine learning models that span the interpretability-flexibility spectrum. The three components can also be used independently, depending on whether interpretability or predictive flexibility is prioritized. The abilities of the proposed method have been tested on real-world use cases in computational medicinal chemistry: an independent set from DrugBank, library screening of Enamine and KLIFS compounds, and de novo molecule generation via REINVENT4. The proposed approach therefore provides a more discriminative, interpretable and target-aware complement to existing drug-likeness scores, suitable for ranking in early discovery pipelines and as a reward function for generative chemistry. Furthermore, a user-friendly web portal (https://huggingface.co/spaces/kochgroup/FamDLike) is available to obtain drug-likeness profiles of molecules.
papers.summary: 全局类药性评分是否适合所有靶标家族？本文摘要指出，不同家族的配体占据不同理化空间，统一标准可能造成系统性奖惩偏差。FamDLike结合期望度函数、广义加性模型和树模型，支持在可解释性与预测灵活性之间选择，并在独立分子集、化合物库筛选及生成任务中测试。其价值在于为生成式药物设计提供靶标感知的评价目标，但摘要未给出量化性能，不能据此认定优于现有方法。[摘要]

raw_metadata.title_zh: 超越全局类药性：面向靶标家族的FamDLike类药性评分框架

article.lead: 同一套类药性标准，是否适合所有靶标家族？FamDLike将靶标家族差异纳入小分子评价，为理解虚拟筛选与生成式分子设计中的评分偏向提供了一个具体切口。

sections.title: 全局类药性标准可能偏向哪些分子？
paragraphs: 类药性评分用于评价小分子的理化特征，既可充当虚拟筛选的过滤条件，也可作为生成式设计的奖励函数。摘要指出，QED等通用评分虽被广泛采用，但不同治疗靶标家族的配体并不占据相同的理化空间。
因此，统一标准可能系统性地奖励某些靶标类别、惩罚另一些类别，使被视为“具有类药性”的化学空间收窄。本文关注的不是取消类药性评价，而是让评价更贴近具体靶标家族及项目需求。

sections.title: 用互补模型刻画家族特异性
paragraphs: FamDLike结合了期望函数、广义加性模型和基于树的机器学习模型，覆盖从可解释性到预测灵活性的不同取向。摘要同时说明，这些组件也可以独立使用，具体取决于使用者更重视哪一方面。
框架旨在更准确地区分靶标家族，并探索各家族特异的类药化学空间。摘要列出的测试场景包括DrugBank独立数据集、Enamine与KLIFS化合物库筛选，以及通过REINVENT4开展的从头分子生成。

sections.title: 摘要报告的是定性优势与应用定位
paragraphs: 作者将FamDLike概括为对既有类药性评分的一种补充，报告其具有更强的区分能力、可解释性和靶标感知能力。不过，摘要没有给出这些优势对应的量化指标、比较幅度或不同模型组件的分项表现。
摘要将早期发现流程中的分子排序和生成化学奖励函数列为适用用途，并说明已提供用于获取分子类药性画像的网页入口。这些表述不应进一步解读为已证明能够提高成药成功率。

sections.title: 测试覆盖与比较强度仍需查阅正文
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断训练与测试样本规模、具体覆盖哪些靶标家族、数据划分及去重方式，也无法确认与QED等评分比较时的指标、基线配置和统计不确定性。这里的信息缺口不等于论文没有开展相关工作。
DrugBank独立数据集及库筛选、生成任务说明了测试场景，但不足以确定跨家族泛化边界，或判断生成分子的活性、安全性与可合成性是否得到验证。当前资料支持的是框架与用途层面的解读。

sections.title: 阅读启发：先审视奖励函数偏好什么
paragraphs: 阅读启发：对生成式设计而言，值得先问评分函数是否把特定类别的偏好当成了普适标准。继续阅读本文时，可重点关注家族特异评分如何改变候选分子的排序，以及可解释性与预测灵活性之间如何取舍；这些问题不预设新评分必然带来更好的分子。

sections.title: 用互补模型刻画家族特异性
paragraphs: FamDLike结合了期望函数、广义加性模型和基于树的机器学习模型，覆盖从可解释性到预测灵活性的不同取向。摘要同时说明，这些组件也可以独立使用，具体取决于使用者更重视哪一方面。
框架旨在更准确地区分靶标家族，并探索各家族特异的类药化学空间。摘要列出的测试场景包括DrugBank独立数据集、Enamine与KLIFS化合物库筛选，以及通过REINVENT4开展的从头分子生成。

sections.title: 摘要报告的是定性优势与应用定位
paragraphs: 作者将FamDLike概括为对既有类药性评分的一种补充，报告其具有更强的区分能力、可解释性和靶标感知能力。不过，摘要没有给出这些优势对应的量化指标、比较幅度或不同模型组件的分项表现。
摘要将早期发现流程中的分子排序和生成化学奖励函数列为适用用途，并说明已提供用于获取分子类药性画像的网页入口。这些表述不应进一步解读为已证明能够提高成药成功率。

sections.title: 测试覆盖与比较强度仍需查阅正文
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断训练与测试样本规模、具体覆盖哪些靶标家族、数据划分及去重方式，也无法确认与QED等评分比较时的指标、基线配置和统计不确定性。这里的信息缺口不等于论文没有开展相关工作。
DrugBank独立数据集及库筛选、生成任务说明了测试场景，但不足以确定跨家族泛化边界，或判断生成分子的活性、安全性与可合成性是否得到验证。当前资料支持的是框架与用途层面的解读。

sections.title: 阅读启发：先审视奖励函数偏好什么
paragraphs: 阅读启发：对生成式设计而言，值得先问评分函数是否把特定类别的偏好当成了普适标准。继续阅读本文时，可重点关注家族特异评分如何改变候选分子的排序，以及可解释性与预测灵活性之间如何取舍；这些问题不预设新评分必然带来更好的分子。

papers.title: QTN-RQNN: Quantum Tensor Network-Based Recurrent Quantum Neural Network
papers.abstract: Resource constraints and imperfect quantum operations remain major challenges for quantum machine learning (QML) on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, particularly for fault-diagnosis tasks involving imbalanced and heterogeneous data. This work proposes QTN-RQNN, a Quantum Tensor Network-Based Recurrent Quantum Neural Network that integrates tensor-network-inspired nearest-neighbor interactions with recurrent quantum processing. The model sequentially encodes input features while propagating quantum memory across recurrent steps and incorporates QSMOTE for class balancing. QTN-RQNN is evaluated on four heterogeneous fault-diagnosis datasets SPID, CWRUBD, EFDD, and SFDD and compared with QNN, QTN-QNN, and RQNN baselines through classification, ablation, multi-seed, convergence, and quantum-resource analyses. Results show dataset-dependent predictive behavior, indicating that increased quantum architectural complexity does not universally improve classification. On SPID, QTN-RQNN improves the RQNN F1-score from 0.3077 to 0.4516 and ROC-AUC from 0.4485 to 0.6970, while the remaining datasets exhibit different performance-resource trade-offs and sensitivity to recurrent timesteps and circuit depth. Across all datasets, QTN-RQNN reduces the two-qubit-gate count from 32 to 24 per sample relative to RQNN, corresponding to a 25% reduction without increasing the four-qubit requirement; the same relative reduction is obtained for QTN-QNN over QNN. These findings establish QTN-RQNN as a resource-conscious recurrent quantum architecture and highlight the need to jointly consider predictive performance and circuit-resource requirements for near-term quantum fault diagnosis.

papers.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
papers.abstract: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

papers.title: Non-destructive imaging and structural techniques for reliability assessment of power electronic modules: A literature review of conventional, automated and machine learning-based approaches
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of electrified transport, renewable energy systems and high-efficiency industrial power converters relies on the robustness of power electronic modules and multi-chip packaging architectures. As module power densities rise and operating environments become more extreme, reliability becomes a key determinant of system lifetime, safety and cost. Thermo-mechanical degradation mechanisms such as die-attach delamination, bond-wire lift-off often initiate within material layers, making non-destructive testing (NDT) essential for quality and health monitoring. This literature review assesses state-of-the-art non-destructive imaging modalities for power electronic modules, with primary focus on IGBT packaging architectures. It covers X-ray imaging, scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM), optical metrology and infrared thermography. Rather than treating these modalities in isolation, it evaluates their compatibility, limits and fault-oriented application ranges. Emphasis is placed on the industry transition from manual evaluation to automated, machine learning-driven workflows for defect segmentation, void quantification and multimodal data fusion. It concludes by outlining industrial best practices, software and hardware bottlenecks and directions for embedding machine learning into autonomous packaging inspection. No single NDT technique provides complete assessment of module health, necessitating the complementary use of multiple modalities. Automation and machine-learning approaches improve defect detection but reamin dependant on physics-based measurements, high-quality data and application-specific workflows.

papers.title: Defect Detection in Rotor-Bearing-Gear Systems for Experimental Frequency-Domain Fault Diagnosis using FFT and Machine Learning Techniques
papers.abstract: Rotor bearing gear system is mostly used in rotating machinery in industries and has considerable susceptibility to defects such as wear, pitting, and failure in gears, corrosion of components, and damage to bearings under different operating conditions. This paper presents an experimental study of fault diagnosis implemented in the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Machine Learning Techniques. In the Experimental study, the bevel gearbox test rig was exercised under various operating conditions (200 rpm to 1000 rpm, loading (20 N to 100 N)), and six types of faults were exercised for each case, including mutually imposed multiple fault conditions. For each fault condition, FFT analysis identified characteristic fault frequencies, harmonics, sidebands, and modulation effects were found by FFT analysis. We observed that as the fault level, speed, and load increased, vibration amplitude increased significantly. Frequency-domain vibration features were used in this study with machine learning classifiers to determine fault conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance applications.

papers.title: Intelligent Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Power Transformers Using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Background: Power transformers play an integral role in power generation and transmission. Transformer failures can lead to service interruptions, reduce system reliability, and incur significant failure-related costs. Efficient transformer maintenance requires accurate condition assessment and effective maintenance decision-making. Objective: The purpose of this paper is to develop a machine-learning-based decision-support framework for power transformer maintenance that integrates health index estimation, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, and Life Cycle Cost (LCC) evaluation. Methods: The framework draws on multimodal monitoring data from 166 oil-immersed power transformers collected over a ten-year period. Six machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Convolutional Neural Networks, Ridge Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors) were evaluated using various feature sets. Results: Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the best performance under the basic feature configuration, with an RMSE of 0.285 years, an MAE of 0.199 years, and an R² of 0.956. The robustness evaluation showed that the model retained satisfactory predictive performance under moderate feature reduction. Based on the Life Cycle Cost assumptions applied in this study, the predictive maintenance scenario was estimated to reduce the total cost of the transformer fleet by approximately 47%. Conclusion: The proposed approach combines accurate RUL prediction with technical and economic analyses to provide a practical decision-making tool for transformer asset management.

papers.title: Bayesian‐Based Mixed‐Integer Optimization for Resonance Fatigue Testing of Large‐Scale Wind Turbine Blades
papers.abstract: Fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades is a critical step in ensuring their operational reliability, however, repeatedly developing loading fixtures for different test phases (such as static and fatigue testing) often entails significant time and financial costs. To achieve reusability of test loading fixtures and comply with the strict load conservative envelope principle specified in the standards, this paper proposes a method for optimizing full‐scale structural fatigue test loading schemes for blades based on Bayesian optimization and mixed‐integer nonlinear programming (MINLP). This method treats the mounting positions of the exciter and counterweight in the fatigue test loading scheme as discrete variables, and optimizes the excitation force amplitude, the mass of the loading saddle at the excitation point, and the mass of the counterweight as continuous variables. In the mixed optimization of discrete and continuous variables, the static test loading points are treated as discrete candidate positions for the fatigue test equipment. The base mass of each static test loading saddle is used as the lower bound for the corresponding mass variable. In the dynamic model optimized for flapwise direction, the stiffness softening effects caused by pre‐bending and geometric nonlinearity is considered. The rationality of the optimized loading scheme was verified through full‐scale structural fatigue testing of 100‐meter‐class wind turbine blades. The results indicate that the optimized loading scheme achieved a global safety envelope for the target design bending moment in both flapwise and edgewise fatigue tests. The maximum positive deviation of the measured bending moment in the flapwise and edgewise directions was controlled at approximately 8.6% and 16.4%, respectively, meeting the certification requirements for equivalent fatigue damage specified in the IEC 61400–23 standard. This optimization method provides a technical framework for designing loading schemes for full‐scale structural fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades that combines theoretical accuracy with cost‐effectiveness. It can effectively reduce the preparation time for large‐scale blade fatigue testing and ensure the rationality of certification.
papers.summary: 大型风电叶片静力与疲劳试验反复配置加载夹具，增加时间和成本。本文结合贝叶斯优化与混合整数非线性规划，联合选择设备安装位置、激振力幅值及配重质量，并利用静力试验加载点促进夹具复用。摘要报告，百米级叶片全尺寸试验实现了目标设计弯矩的安全包络，挥舞与摆振方向最大正偏差约为8.6%和16.4%。该研究适合关注疲劳试验设计与认证可靠性的读者，但当前仅有摘要，算法细节及成本收益尚无法核对。[摘要]

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Fatigue Detection From EEG Signals: A Methodological Pilot Framework With Potential For Nursing Applications
papers.venue: Journal of Clinical Practice and Research
papers.abstract: Objective: Fatigue is a significant occupational health issue that adversely affects attention and decision-making. This study aimed to objectively predict fatigue levels using EEG signals and machine learning models and to develop a physiologically based assessment framework with potential future applications in nursing. Materials and Methods: Time-domain, frequency-domain, entropy, Hjorth, and wavelet features were extracted from EEG data collected from 12 participants aged 21-40 years, with fatigue levels labeled using various scales. Results: Classification performance varied across validation strategies. Under 5-fold cross-validation, Random Forest achieved the highest performance (accuracy=1.00, macro-F1=1.00), while KNN and NB also demonstrated strong performance. However, under LOOCV, sensitivity, precision, and macro-F1 values decreased despite relatively high accuracy. LOSO validation yielded more balanced results, with Random Forest maintaining the best performance (accuracy=0.97, macro-F1=0.91). Conclusion: EEG-derived features provide valuable information for fatigue assessment. Although high performance was achieved under certain validation strategies, subject-independent evaluation revealed more realistic performance levels. The proposed framework offers a practical approach to fatigue monitoring. Future studies should focus on larger, domain-specific datasets and multimodal integration to enhance generalizability.

papers.title: Machine-learning-assisted quantum photonics: from emitter control to integration
papers.abstract: Discovering unconventional optical designs via machine-learning promises to advance on-chip circuitry, imaging, sensing, energy, and quantum information technology. In this talk, we discuss photonic design approaches and emerging material platforms for showcasing machine-learning-assisted topology optimization for optical metasurface designs with applications in thermophotovoltaics, reflective optics, quantum photonic circuitry and lightsail technology. We demonstrate the effectiveness of autoencoders for compressing the vast design space of metasurfaces into a smaller search space. By employing global optimization via adjoint methods or quantum annealing, one can find the optimal metasurface designs within the smaller space constructed by the autoencoder. The techniques employed in this work extend well beyond the metasurface optimization space and into many inverse design problems for engineering and physics. We also apply machine learning approaches to advance quantum measurements and imaging.

papers.title: Development and interpretability of a machine learning-derived model for predicting the risk of subsequent short-term infection in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Infections are a major cause of mortality in hemodialysis patients, but early risk stratification remains difficult. This study developed and validated an interpretable ML model using routine baseline laboratory data to predict short-term infection risk. Methods A retrospective cohort of 622 hemodialysis patients with uremia was analyzed. The primary outcome was a confirmed infectious event (infection, sepsis, or pneumonia) occurring within a 2-month follow-up. To rigorously prevent data leakage, the cohort was strictly partitioned into training (70%) and test (30%) sets prior to missing value imputation and any downstream preprocessing. A LightGBM-based forward feature selection was executed exclusively within the training set. Nine ML algorithms were evaluated, and model robustness was validated via nested cross-validation, repeated cross-validation, and bootstrap optimism correction. Interpretability was achieved using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results Subsequent infections occurred in 157 patients (25.2%). A parsimonious six-biomarker signature (CysC, HCT, TP, MONO_pct, MYO, ADA) was identified. The K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and LightGBM models demonstrated robust discriminative performance (Test AUROC: 0.727 and 0.719, respectively). Nested cross-validation confirmed generalization stability (e.g., ANN mean AUC: 0.722). SHAP analysis revealed elevated Cystatin C and lowered Hematocrit as the strongest contributors to the model’s risk ranking. Although the model showed high ranking ability, the default 0.5 threshold yielded low sensitivity; a prespecified F2‑optimized threshold of 0.30 improved sensitivity to 0.723 in the test set. Conclusion This interpretable machine learning‑based predictive model, using routinely available laboratory data, may serve as a potential adjunctive decision‑support tool for stratifying short‑term infection risk. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Methods for Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis: Optimization and Comparison
papers.abstract: Rolling bearings are the vital support elements of industrial rotating machinery. Operational conditions have a direct impact on the safety, dependability and economical operation and maintenance of the production system. An effective and accurate fault diagnosis technology is very important for predictive maintenance and reducing the probability of downtime. With the development of deep learning and signal processing technologies, intelligent fault diagnosis based on vibration signals has become a research hotspot, and various technical methods and implementation schemes have been proposed. In this paper, three traditional deep-learning-based approaches for the diagnosis of rolling bearing faults are systematically studied, including the time-frequency image diagnosis method based on the ICEEMDAN decomposition integrated with the Hilbert transform and CBAM - ResNet, the FSCL diagnosis model combining FFT + SVD with CNN - LSTM, and the classification framework fusing the continuous wavelet transform signal-to-image conversion with SE-ResNet. This paper also discusses the technical frameworks and effectiveness of each approach. In this study, the inherent limitations of the three approaches were systematically studied from pre-processing efficiency, model complexity, end-user adaptability and generalization ability of scenarios, and relevant optimization strategies were put forward. The research results can be used as reference to promote the technology progress and industrial application of intelligent fault diagnosis for rolling bearings.

papers.title: CTML: A Comprehensive Framework for Continuous Testing in Machine Learning Operations
papers.abstract: The increasing use of machine learning (ML) systems in production has highlighted some important weaknesses in traditional software testing methods. Unlike regular software, ML systems can fail in specific ways due to their reliance on data, including issues like data drift, concept drift, and performance decline. To address these issues, this paper introduces the Continuous Testing for Machine Learning (CTML) framework. This framework is designed specifically for MLOps environments and offers a thorough, automated solution. It establishes a standardized way to evaluate ML systems across four main areas: data quality, drift detection, model quality, and pipeline validation. The CTML framework consists of a modular setup that includes a Test Registry, Test Runner, Result Store, and Integration Layer. This design ensures it integrates smoothly with existing Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines and MLOps platforms. We put this framework to the test in a predictive maintenance case study, which showed how effective it is at identifying issues like data drift, performance degradation, and bottlenecks in the pipeline problems that traditional testing methods might overlook. The findings indicate that CTML successfully uncovers critical failures in the system across all testing dimensions, providing useful insights to help keep ML systems running smoothly in production. Overall, this work presents a new, integrated framework that connects academic research with industry best practices, pushing forward the standards in MLOps quality assurance.

papers.title: Topology Optimization and Generative Design in Additive Manufacturing: A Systematic Review of Algorithms, Tools and Industrial Applications
papers.venue: Open Access Research Journal of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has increased the design space of engineering components, allowing the creation of geometries which are hard or even impossible to realise through conventional machining, casting and forming. The capacity has added to the curiosity surrounding generative design (GD) and topology optimisation (TO), which aim to enhance structural performance, minimise material consumption and investigate other design options. This review combines the technical compilation provided with the relevant scholarly literature on the relationship between TO, GD and AM. The review is organised around the reporting principles of PRISMA 2020 and focuses specifically on the review question, eligibility logic, organisation of the evidence, methodological limitations and research gaps. Literature suggests that density-based approaches like Solid Isotropic Material with Penalisation (SIMP), level-set methods and evolutionary techniques continue to be important TO approaches, and GD is a broader requirements-driven approach which can involve optimisation, simulation, materials selection, and manufacturing constraints. The key result here is that having the best solution in the world of computation does not guarantee the best solution in the world of manufacturing, economy and reliability. All of these, such as overhangs, support structure, build orientation, enclosed voids, minimum feature size, anisotropy, residual stress, thermal distortion, surface finish, post-processing and cost, need to be taken into consideration in the design process. Applications in the aerospace, automotive and lightweight cellular structures sectors show promising potential, but benefits have only been reported in the context of specific applications. The next step in research should focus on coupled design–process optimisation, multi-physics modelling, uncertainty quantification, explainable artificial intelligence, experimental validation and closed-loop digital manufacturing. The synthesis is also embedded in the setting of an industrial economy, where knowledge and skills about the processes, their parameters and constraints determine what can be practically achieved, and in which limited use of AM and simulation tools is prevalent. The review finds that the maturity of TO and GD should be assessed based on the quality of validated engineering outcomes and not just on the geometric complexity or weight reduction alone.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Tool Condition Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance in CNC Machining: A Systematic Review
papers.venue: Open Access Research Journal of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining is the backbone of precision manufacturing, but the productivity, part quality and machine uptime of CNC machining are dependent on the condition of the cutting tool. Conventional fixed-interval tool replacement either discards valuable tool life or permits the tool to be used past safe bounds of dimension, and progressive flank wear, chipping and breakage also affect surface finish and dimensional accuracy. This systematic review follows the reporting guidelines outlined in the PRISMA 2020 statement, and summarizes the existing research literature between January 2016 and September 2026 addressing the application of machine learning (ML) for CNC tool condition monitoring (TCM) and predictive maintenance (PdM). Studies were classified along four dimensions: machining operation, sensing modality, learning method and maintenance objective. It has been revealed that cutting force, vibration, acoustic emission and spindle current/power are the most important indirect measurement signals; that feature quality has significant influence on the performance of traditional classifiers; and that the deep sequence model, including convolutional and long short-term memory models, is now the most popular model for wear estimation and remaining useful life prediction. The reported accuracy is generally in the range of 85% to 99%, but is rarely comparable because the datasets, tools, materials, and validation procedures vary. The research gaps identified were: lack of or costly labelled data, poor cross-machine generalisation, real-time deployment latency, class imbalance and data quality, limited interpretability, under-used ensemble and hybrid methods, under-representation of small firms and developing economies, and incompleteness in integrating with digital twins and CAD/CAM data. The review suggests a research agenda, in which transferable and explainable models are coupled with design-of-experiments process knowledge, low-cost edge sensing and human-centred implementation, particularly relevant for manufacturers operating in resource constrained industrial environments

papers.title: Beyond Threshold Protection: Leakage-Safe and Protection-Aware Machine Learning for Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Variable-Frequency Drives
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A reproducible simulation-derived benchmark for leakage-safe and protection-aware fault diagnosis in industrial variable-frequency drives. The release contains 384 scenarios across eight balanced classes, 2,304 diagnostic windows with 20 measurement-derived features, 11,520 rolling windows, scenario-isolated and operating-point-held-out partitions, anti-aliased time/frequency tensors, classical and neural baselines, calibrated uncertainty, robustness analysis, attribution evidence, and conventional protection-rule comparators. The authoritative neural workflow uses a deterministic single-thread CPU reference runtime. The deposited files are restricted during peer review. Editors and reviewers may access the complete benchmark through a private read-only Zenodo sharing link supplied by the corresponding author.

papers.title: Biaxial tension-torsion coupling fatigue resonance of single-walled MoS2 nanotubes.
papers.abstract: Fatigue characteristics of nanotubes are crucial for enhancing the reliability of flexible nanoelectronic devices. This work systematically investigates fatigue behaviors of single-walled MoS2 nanotubes subjected to biaxial tensile-torsion coupling loading. Results show that fatigue life decreases as torsion angle and axial excitation frequency increase. More interestingly, fatigue life exhibits a non-monotonic decrease with increasing excitation frequency for all torsion angles, presenting two distinct minima in the low-to-mid frequency range. We have developed a method for calculating natural frequencies under combined biaxial tension and torsion, and discovered that the first minimum corresponds to the tensile natural frequency, while the second corresponds to its first harmonic. In the high-frequency regime, however, fatigue life rapidly drops into a broad minimum plateau governed by strain-rate effects rather than sharp harmonic resonances. Namely, the minimum of these two fatigue lives is caused by fatigue resonance due to excitation frequency being equal to the system's natural frequency. We also find that fatigue energy is distributed and dissipated at the excitation frequency and natural frequency. When excitation frequency matches the natural frequency, fatigue life reaches a minimum due to the dissipation of most natural frequency phonons. These observations provide guidance for considering fatigue resonance under tension-torsion coupling to improve the service life of nanotube-based devices.

article.lead: 单壁 MoS₂ 纳米管在双轴拉伸—扭转耦合作用下，会在临界频率处出现疲劳寿命急降。这项研究提示，理解疲劳风险不能忽略耦合载荷下的共振现象。

sections.title: 拉伸与扭转耦合下的疲劳问题
paragraphs: 本次可核验摘要聚焦单壁 MoS₂ 纳米管，讨论双轴拉伸—扭转耦合与疲劳共振之间的关系。其关注点不仅是纳米管是否发生疲劳，还包括临界频率处寿命骤降这一现象，为理解频率相关的疲劳风险提供了明确切入点。

sections.title: 摘要明确了载荷情境，未展开研究方法
paragraphs: 摘要明确给出的研究情境是双轴拉伸—扭转耦合作用，但未说明具体采用实验、数值模拟还是理论分析，也未交代加载程序及疲劳寿命的判定方式。因此，当前不能据此还原研究流程，或介绍固有频率的计算方法。

sections.title: 临界频率处出现疲劳寿命急降
paragraphs: 摘要报告，双轴拉伸—扭转耦合会在单壁 MoS₂ 纳米管中引发强烈的疲劳共振，并导致临界频率处的寿命急剧下降。当前资料支持这一现象性结论，但未给出临界频率的位置、寿命下降幅度或完整的频率响应变化，不能进一步补写定量结果。

sections.title: 样本、比较与验证范围仍待确认
paragraphs: 仅凭本次可核验摘要，无法判断研究的样本规模、纳米管几何与材料参数、载荷取值、具体比较对象及验证范围，也无法确认结果能否推广至其他结构或器件工况。这些属于当前摘要未提供的信息，并不意味着论文没有开展相应分析或验证。

sections.title: 阅读启发：关注寿命急降的适用条件
paragraphs: 阅读启发：进一步阅读时，值得优先确认临界频率如何识别、疲劳共振如何得到支持，以及寿命急降对应哪些拉伸与扭转条件。对疲劳可靠性研究而言，这有助于理解结论的适用边界，而不能直接据此宣称某种器件寿命改进已经得到验证。

papers.title: Explainable Failure Prediction and Prevention in Maritime
papers.abstract: Maritime systems operate in highly dynamic environments where unexpected equipment failures can compromise safety, reliability, and operational efficiency. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, digital twins, and predictive maintenance enable proactive failure prediction and prevention. However, ensuring trustworthy and explainable decision-making remains a major challenge in safety-critical maritime applications. This chapter reviews key AI technologies required for explainable failure prediction and prevention in maritime systems and presents a conceptual architecture capable of supporting autonomous or human-in-the-loop corrective actions. This architecture integrates data acquisition, time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, risk assessment, decision-making, and explainable AI into a closed-loop framework. With reference to the architectural components, a review and discussion of relevant maritime studies is performed, outlining their methods, advantages, and limitations. Furthermore, it highlights current challenges, including uncertainty and robustness, model generalization, explainability, limited availability of maritime datasets, and operational deployment, and identifies future research directions toward trustworthy AI-assisted maritime decision-making.

papers.title: Thermo-vibrational fusion for early-stage ball bearing fault diagnosis: a multi-modal machine learning framework
papers.venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
papers.abstract: Abstract Rolling bearing failures account for 40–50% of rotating machinery breakdowns, but the complementary diagnostic potential of thermal sensing remains underutilized. This study presents a thermo-vibrational fusion framework for early-stage ball bearing fault diagnosis using the KAIST run-to-failure dataset (128 h, NSK 6205 bearing). A 40-dimensional feature vector comprising FFT-based spectral features at the bearing defect frequencies (BPFO, BPFI, BSF), sub-band energy ratios, spectral entropy, and six time-domain statistical descriptors across all four sensor channels is extracted. Three classifiers – SVM, Random Forest, and DNN – are evaluated under five-fold stratified cross-validation. The DNN achieves 95.7% accuracy (AUC = 0.983), RF 94.1% (AUC = 0.975), and SVM 91.3% (AUC = 0.961). Feature importance analysis confirms vibration kurtosis (14.2%) and bearing temperature RMS (5.8%) as the most discriminative features, validating the multi-modal approach. On this dataset, acquired under constant speed and load, thermal features preceded an unambiguous vibration RMS escalation by 15–25 h during incipient degradation, improving early-stage precision by 4–6% points over vibration-only classification. The novelty of the work lies in providing the first quantitative characterisation of this thermal-to-vibration diagnostic lead time on a publicly available, fully synchronised run-to-failure dataset, benchmarked across three classifier families under an identical leakage-free protocol with physically grounded feature attribution; the transfer of these findings to variable-speed and fluctuating-load environments is discussed as a limitation of the present study.

papers.title: Therapeutic peptide informatics in the artificial intelligence era: From curated resources to generative design.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides are emerging as a powerful class of pharmaceuticals that combine the synthetic accessibility of small molecules with the specificity of biologics, yet poor stability and low oral bioavailability remain barriers. This review surveys an expanded, scope-defined set of 39 therapeutic peptide databases and 62 computational tools for activity prediction, physicochemical profiling, structural modeling and rational design. We highlight how machine learning and deep learning are accelerating data-driven peptide drug discovery and discuss the urgent need for standardized data frameworks and integrated evaluation platforms to bridge the gap between computational prediction and experimental validation.

papers.title: Machine learning for high-performance alloy design: A review
papers.abstract: The traditional trial-and-error paradigm in alloy design, which has become too slow and resource-intensive, is increasingly inadequate for meeting the rapid industrial demand for high-performance materials. Recently, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a transformative and cost-effective approach to accelerate the discovery and optimization of advanced alloys by efficiently mining large datasets to uncover hidden patterns. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental algorithms, typical workflows, and recent advancements in ML-driven alloy design. We systematically examine the application of data-driven models in bridging the complex composition-process-microstructure-property linkages. By capturing these intricate relationships, ML enables the precise quantitative prediction of phase constitution, precipitation behavior, mechanical properties, and long-term service performance. Furthermore, we highlight advanced strategies for the joint optimization of both composition and processing parameters. We specifically detail the paradigm shift from traditional forward prediction-driven screening to target-oriented inverse design and multi-objective optimization, which allow researchers to input desired performance metrics and directly generate the optimal alloy recipes. The efficacy and practical value of these ML frameworks are clearly demonstrated through their successful deployment in discovering and refining representative high-performance systems. Finally, we discuss the current challenges in the field and propose future perspectives for developing robust, interpretable, and closed-loop intelligent high-performance alloy design frameworks.

papers.title: Machine learning for fault detection, diagnosis, anomaly detection and failure prediction in industrial electric motors and fans: protocol for an AI-assisted systematic review of openly accessible studies with real-time or field elements
papers.abstract: This project registers the protocol of an AI-assisted systematic review prepared for a master's thesis (Information Technologies, LBTU) on predictive maintenance of industrial devices. Purpose: To map how openly accessible primary studies published 2015–2026 develop, train, validate and deploy machine-learning models for fault detection, fault diagnosis, anomaly detection and failure prediction in industrial electric motors and fans, when the models run in real time, on embedded/edge or IoT systems, with a digital twin, or on field data from machines in operation. Methods: Searches of OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv (titles/abstracts; search strings validated with known-item recall and sampled precision), plus review-based citation searching. Title/abstract screening by an AI model in two independent passes with adjudication, checked against the author's blinded decisions (percent agreement, Cohen's kappa, PABAK). Full-text eligibility and data extraction from legal open-access full texts, with every judgement anchored to a quoted text snippet. Extracted items: machines, components and fault types; signals, datasets and fault origin (simulated, laboratory-seeded, run-to-failure, field); model families and techniques; training and validation design, including data-leakage risks; real-time and deployment characteristics (online inference, latency, edge/cloud, deployment level). Risk of bias is rated with a tool adapted for ML studies on machine data. Synthesis is a structured narrative synthesis (SWiM) with descriptive statistics; no meta-analysis is planned. Expected outcomes: (1) a map of the machines, data, models and training/validation practices used in real-time and field-oriented ML predictive maintenance of motors and fans; (2) estimates of how often validation designs and data-leakage risks support or undermine reported performance; (3) the state of real-time deployment and the barriers studies report; (4) evidence-traced design implications and candidate requirements for a real-time predictive-maintenance system for industrial motor–fan drive trains, which feed the practical chapters of the thesis. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, PRISMA-trAIce (AI use) and SWiM. AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) is disclosed in full, with prompts archived. The frozen protocol and supporting files are attached.

papers.title: Integrating Survival-Based Aging Models with Data-Driven RUL Prognostics
papers.abstract: Predictive maintenance requires reliable remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. Existing methods mainly follow two paradigms: wear-based aging models that capture cumulative degradation and sensor-driven data models that reflect instantaneous health conditions, each providing only partial information. In this work, we propose a probabilistic fusion framework that integrates wear-based and sensor-based prognostic components through failure probability distributions. Based on explicit structural assumptions linking wear, latent health, sensor observations, and failure, we derive a principled combination rule that enables uncertainty-aware integration with adaptive weighting of the components. Experimentally, we assess this combination rule by learning the wear-based component using a parametric survival model and the sensor-based component using a 1D convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) with a post-hoc uncertainty model. Evaluation on multiple N-CMAPSS datasets demonstrates that the fused model improves point accuracy, preserves the C-index, and produces narrower yet well-calibrated prediction intervals compared to either component alone. The results highlight the complementary roles of wear-based survival model and sensor-based deep learning model, and show that their probabilistic integration provides a structured pathway toward more robust and consistent prognostics over the life-time.

papers.title: Drugging the Undruggable in Oncology: Structural Computation, Machine Learning, and Generative AI for Historically Intractable Targets
papers.abstract: For four decades the central oncogenic drivers of human cancer the RAS GTPases, the transcription-factor MYC, mutant p53, and the protein-tyrosine phosphatases, fusion oncoproteins and intrinsically disordered regulators that surround them were regarded as undruggable: lacking deep, well-defined small-molecule binding pockets, governed by femtomolar substrate affinities, or driven through flat protein–protein interfaces that classical medicinal chemistry could not engage. The last decade has overturned that verdict. This narrative review argues that the convergence of three advances has made the undruggable proteome systematically approachable: the discovery of cryptic, allosteric and induced pockets through molecular dynamics and deep learning; the maturation of physics-based and machine-learned models that can read out binding from structure; and the rise in generative artificial intelligence that can design novel molecules conditioned directly on a three-dimensional target. We develop the argument in full formal detail. We set out the mathematics of modern molecular machine learning E(3)/SE(3)-equivariant graph neural networks, denoising diffusion and score-based generative models, and generative flow networks alongside the statistical mechanics of binding free energy (free-energy perturbation, thermodynamic integration, MM-PBSA), the kinetics of covalent inhibition, the equilibrium theory of ternary complexes and cooperativity that governs molecular glues and degraders, and the pharmacology that determines whether a designed molecule reaches and acts on a tumour. We then examine, target by target, the biology that made each oncoprotein intractable and the campaigns structural, chemical and increasingly computational that have begun to defeat it, distinguishing throughout what classical structural and computational work achieved, what machine learning demonstrably contributed, and what generative design has so far only promised: the switch-II pocket and the covalent KRAS-G12C and non-covalent KRAS-G12D and pan-RAS(ON) inhibitors; the mutation-created cavity of p53-Y220C and its first reactivators; the disordered MYC-MAX interface and the miniprotein Omomyc; and the allosteric tunnel of SHP2. These four are selected for mechanistic non-redundancy, on grounds we state explicitly, and the structured search framework and eligibility criteria underlying the review are documented. We foreground the newest evidence AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold All-Atom, deep cryptic-pocket predictors, and the first generative-to-clinic existence proofs while maintaining candour about the field’s hard limits: the physical-validity and generalisation gaps of deep docking, the bounded accuracy and cost of free-energy methods, the synthesizability gap, dual-use risk, and a clinical attrition that artificial intelligence has not yet reduced. The synthesis we offer is not that the problem is solved but that it has changed in kind: from a search for the rare tractable target to the deliberate, computable engineering of molecules against targets once thought beyond reach.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Machines
papers.venue: Journal of Bioengineering, Technologies and Health
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel approach to constructing a predictive model using machine learning techniques for the early identification of machine faults for industrial maintenance purposes. The topic is justified by the importance of predictive maintenance in increasing operational efficiency, reducing costs, and improving the reliability of industrial equipment. The early identification of failures makes it possible to carry out preventive interventions, avoiding negative consequences and optimizing the use of industrial resources. Traditional maintenance techniques, such as corrective and preventive maintenance based on fixed intervals, cannot adequately predict unexpected events that could lead to equipment failure. The main objective is to develop and validate a predictive model capable of detecting patterns that indicate possible failures in industrial machinery before they occur. To this end, a hybrid algorithm combining fuzzy logic and machine learning will be applied compared to three traditional models widely used in the literature. The study includes a comparative analysis of the results obtained, evaluating the performance, accuracy, and effectiveness of each model. The advantages and limitations of the developed model will also be discussed, as well as suggestions for future research to improve predictive systems in the sector continuously. This article is divided into sections, starting with the introduction, with a general contextualization of the problem, the arguments, the justifications, the objective, and the structure of the work. The following section presents research into related work. Then the methodology used to develop the fault prediction, and identification models will be presented, followed by the experimental results, and finally the conclusions.

papers.title: ThermoVision-MOSFET: A Multimodal Thermal–Radiographic Machine Learning Framework for Fault Diagnosis and Maintenance Decision Support in Power MOSFETs
papers.venue: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal
papers.abstract: The reliability of power-electronic, automotive, and industrial systems relies on reliable fault detection in the Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors (MOSFETs). Single-modality inspection is still limited as infrared thermography has only surface thermal anomalies, while X-ray radiography has internal structural defects. The paper proposes an integrated diagnostic framework, called ThermoVision-MOSFET, which integrates thermal infrared imaging, X-ray imaging, pre-processing, hybrid segmentation, multi-domain feature extraction, and machine-learning classification. The segmentation pipeline combines the Otsu and adaptive thresholding with the Canny and Sobel edge detection and marker-guided watershed refinement to enhance fault-region localization. Random Forest is used to classify a 28 feature representation that contains statistical, texture, thermal-gradient, morphological, X-ray structural and fusion features. The framework was evaluated on a dataset of 400 MOSFET samples from four diagnosis classes, yielding a segmentation accuracy of 94.7%, classification accuracy of 96.8%, an F1-score of 95.9%, and an AUC of 0.978. The segmentation method proposed in this work outperformed the next best individual method by 9.5 percentage points, and the hybrid thermal-radiographic analysis showed a detection rate of 93.7%–97.6% for six physical fault manifestations. With the highest noise level, segmentation accuracy was 84.1% and the processing time was about 0.47 s per image. The statistical comparisons revealed that the results were significantly better than the individual segmentation baselines (p < 0.01), and the measured throughput suggests the application of moderate throughput diagnostic inspection and assessment for maintenance could be realized in near real-time. The results illustrate the benefit of using multimodal evidence for the diagnosis of MOSFETs and for maintenance-oriented decision making based on condition-based inspection, planned maintenance and prioritized maintenance.

papers.title: Predicting Faults in Mechanical Systems Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
papers.venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: The occurrence of unexpected malfunctions of mechanical systems such as bearings, gearboxes, turbofan engines, and other rotating machinery is still the main cause of downtime, safety hazards, and maintenance cost throughout the manufacturing, energy, and transportation sectors. Recent technological advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technology have transformed fault prediction from an entirely physics-based activity to a data-based activity, in which sensors, signal processing, and learning algorithms estimate the health state of a machine together. This paper provides a structured assessment and comparative synthesis of AI/ML fault-prediction literature. Nineteen peer-reviewed studies obtained from scholarly and web-based databases for the period 2011–2026 are reviewed. A review of the two main tasks: fault diagnosis – classification of fault type, location and severity – prognosis – prediction of remaining useful life, RUL. The evidence is structured into a six-stage pipeline – data acquisition, pre-processing, feature extraction, model training, output, maintenance decision. The analysis is conducted using various test rigs including the CWRU bearings as well as NASA C-MAPSS turbofan engines and gearbox. The results show that on these benchmarks, convolutional and recurrent deep architectures, attention-augmented LSTMs, and ensemble methods consistently outperform classical classifiers; root-mean-square errors (RMSE) on C-MAPSS RUL errors are about 12 cycles and classification accuracies on CWRU exceed 98%. Simultaneously, the review also outlines a number of ongoing open challenges, like data scarcity, domain shift, class imbalance, limited interpretability, and overoptimistic evaluation, which must be overcome before lab results can become consistent with the reliable deployment in the industry. To conclude the paper suggests a standardized benchmarking of multi-fidelity methodologies and explainability-augmented models.

papers.title: Machine learning based geological modelling and application
papers.venue: PolyU Institutional Research Archive (Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
papers.abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of China's economy and the advancement of modernization construction, the demand for underground space development has been increasing day by day, which has also attracted more and more attention from scholars to the problem of geological profile prediction. Accurate geological profile prediction can reveal the distribution characteristics of soil types and strata in a site, which has a significant impact on the design and construction in geotechnical engineering structures. However, the uncertainty and inherent variability of geological formations make accurate geological profile prediction based on sparse borehole data a highly challenging problem. This study proposes two machine learning algorithms based on sparse boreholes for accurate prediction of geological profiles, each with its own advantages. These algorithms are applied to the prediction of geological profiles in multiple practical engineering projects, obtaining accurate geological profiles to guide engineering practice. Comparing the predictions of the proposed algorithm with those from other machine learning methods to demonstrate its superior performance, particularly in significantly improving boundary accuracy. Furthermore, by evaluating the differences between simulated and monitored surface settlements outside the foundation pit by comparing a linearly interpolated geological model with a machine learning-derived nonlinear profile, both based on sparse borehole data. The actual monitoring data shows that the machine learning-predicted nonlinear geology leads to more accurate finite element simulations. The main contributions and innovative achievements of this study are as follows: (1) The MSRF-XGBoost algorithm was proposed, which includes two parts: classification module and filtering module. The classification module is based on the traditional XGBoost algorithm and adds multi receptive field sampling to learn spatial features of different scales between sparse boreholes, enabling accurate prediction of geological profiles through sparse equidistant boreholes alone; The filtering module automatically selects the optimal prediction result from different results predicted by spatial features at different scales through Gaussian filtering, boundary similarity comparison, and other steps. This algorithm solves the dependence of existing machine learning algorithms on training profiles and improves the boundary accuracy of prediction results by about 40% in nonlinear geological profile prediction. (2) An improved GCN algorithm has been proposed. By improving and optimizing the feature expression, adjacency matrix design, and model training method of the GCN algorithm, the improved GCN algorithm can predict the soil type of unknown points through their coordinates, and thus predict the complete geological profile, solving the problem of existing machine learning algorithms relying on equidistant drilling for training. This algorithm can predict accurate geological profiles through sparse non equidistant boreholes. Compared with other machine learning methods, the boundary accuracy of nonlinear geological profile prediction has been improved by about 30%. (3) The two proposed machine learning methods are applied to multiple practical engineering projects. Validation through borehole accuracy assessment of verification boreholes shows prediction accuracy between 80%-99% across three different prediction profiles. Comparative analysis with other machine learning algorithms confirms the proposed methods' advantages in reducing training data requirements while improving prediction accuracy. (4) Taking a foundation pit in Hangzhou as an example, linear geological profiles based on sparse boreholes linear interpolation and nonlinear geological profile finite element models based on algorithm prediction are established. During the simulation of excavation process, the non-linear geological profile finite element model showed a difference of 2% between the surface settlement value outside the pit and the actual monitored settlement value, while the linear geological profile finite element model simulation result differed from the actual settlement value by 12%, indicating that accurate non-linear geological profiles can make finite element model simulation more accurate.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Surface Roughness Prediction of Drilled Hole Surfaces Using Texture and Chip Morphology Features
papers.abstract: Surface roughness ( ) is a significant quality indicator in machined components, influencing performance, fatigue life, and tribological behaviour. Conventional contact-based stylus profilometers are slow, risk micro-scratches, and are impractical for real-time measurement of the surfaces of internally drilled holes. This study proposes a Machine Learning (ML)-based framework that estimates from image-derived texture features, machining parameters, and chip morphology descriptors—specifically addressing drilled hole interiors where curvature and non-uniform illumination render standard planar analysis ineffective. Three models were evaluated: (i) Linear Regression (LR) with GLCM texture features ( = 0.7621); (ii) Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) combining image texture features with spindle speed and feed rate ( = 0.8201, MAE=0.1425 µm); and (iii) XGBoost using chip morphology features with chip area and curl index extracted from chip images ( = 0.8092). A dataset of 370 drilled-hole images of Al-7075 alloy was augmented to 1800 samples. One-way ANOVA confirmed statistically significant performance differences between models (F (2,537) = 47.3, p<0.001). A Streamlit-based interface enables real-time, non-contact prediction at ~45 ms per image, reducing inspection time, cost, and reliance on contact methods.
papers.summary: 钻孔内表面粗糙度影响加工质量与疲劳寿命，但接触式测量难以实时实施。本文以Al-7075合金钻孔图像为对象，比较纹理线性回归、融合纹理与加工参数的XGBoost及切屑形态XGBoost。摘要报告融合模型MAE为0.1425 µm，界面预测约45 ms/图像，并给出模型差异的统计检验。当前仅有摘要，无法核实数据划分与增广流程；其价值在于提供非接触质量估计路径，而非证明疲劳寿命预测能力。[摘要]

papers.title: Thermo-mechanical topology optimization using neural networks with gradient injection
papers.abstract: Abstract Topology optimization using neural networks (TOuNN) parameterizes the density field via a compact fully-connected network and performs design updates through automatic differentiation, ensuring mesh independence and smooth boundaries. Existing TOuNN frameworks are restricted to purely mechanical problems. Under thermo-mechanical coupling, the compliance sensitivity acquires additional contributions from thermal stress and thermal conductivity, which the original loss function cannot capture. This paper proposes a gradient-injected scalar loss that decomposes the total adjoint sensitivity by treating finite-element state quantities (strain energy, temperature, and adjoint temperature) as constants and isolating the differentiable SIMP interpolation functions. During the forward pass, the loss evaluates to the normalized compliance; during backpropagation, its gradient recovers the full three-path adjoint sensitivity. The approach requires neither an end-to-end differentiable finite element solver nor hand-coded backpropagation rules, amounting to a minimal modification of existing TOuNN implementations. Numerical experiments on a half-MBB beam and a cantilever beam demonstrate that the method produces crisp topologies, exhibits robust convergence in the tested cases, and effectively captures the transition from mechanically dominated to thermally dominated behavior.

papers.title: Machine Learning–Based Predictive Maintenance for Semiconductor Fabrication Equipment: Failure Modes, Data Challenges, and Yield Impact
papers.venue: American Journal of Data Science and Analytics
papers.abstract: This study quantitatively evaluated the effectiveness of machine-learning-based predictive maintenance for improving equipment reliability, failure prediction, maintenance efficiency, and production performance in semiconductor fabrication equipment. A longitudinal and quasi-experimental design was applied to an integrated dataset comprising 118 semiconductor manufacturing and supporting equipment units. Following data-quality screening, 2,342,816 equipment-cycle records, 17,923,648 sensor observations, 1,286,540 wafer-processing runs, 9,742 maintenance events, and 2,184 verified failures were retained, with overall data completeness reaching 98.7%. Data challenges were substantial: failure-related observations represented only 1.9% of condition observations, and 143,904 records (5.8%) were excluded because of missing measurements, duplication, timestamp inconsistency, uncertain failure labels, or nonproduction status. Equipment-condition analysis showed that vibration intensity had the strongest relationship with failure occurrence (r = .61; β = .34), followed by alarm frequency (r = .58), vacuum deterioration (r = .55), and temperature deviation (r = .52), with all major relationships significant at p < .001. Failure-mode profiles differed by equipment category: progressive vibration, thermal, pressure, and vacuum degradation in vacuum and pump systems provided the longest median warning lead time (52.7 hours), whereas more abrupt failures in ion implantation provided the shortest (26.8 hours). Conventional machine-learning and deep-learning models were compared using classification, discrimination, and remaining-useful-life metrics. The CNN-LSTM hybrid achieved the strongest independent-test performance, with 97.8% accuracy, 96.4% precision, 96.1% recall, an F1-score of .963, ROC-AUC of .994, and PR-AUC of .979. Remaining-useful-life prediction achieved an MAE of 7.4 hours, RMSE of 11.2 hours, and R² of .94, with a median warning lead time of 41.6 hours. AI-supported predictive maintenance reduced unplanned downtime by 38.5%, failure frequency by 33.3%, emergency repairs by 41.0%, and MTTR by 30.9%, while MTBF increased by 50.0%. Equipment availability increased from 93.1% to 96.5%, and overall equipment effectiveness increased from 75.9% to 81.6%. Degraded equipment conditions increased wafer defect density by 75.0%, reduced throughput by 12.6%, and increased cycle time by 25.2%, whereas predictive maintenance substantially moderated these adverse effects. Yield impact was largest for plasma etching, where degradation increased defect density by 68.4% and reduced first-pass yield by 4.6 percentage points. Temporal and cross-equipment validation confirmed comparatively stable model performance. Generalization to previously unseen equipment remained a data challenge, with accuracy declining from 97.8% to 96.2%.

papers.title: Artificial Neural Network and Machine Learning-Based Diagnosis of Bearing Faults in Turbogenerator System
papers.abstract: This study investigates advanced diagnostic techniques for predicting bearing faults in industrial turbogenerators using Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and Support Vector Regression (SVR). Real-world data were collected from a 58 MW steam-driven turbogenerator over a two-year period, including vibration and rotational speed measurements, to evaluate the reliability of predictive maintenance strategies. A threshold-based monitoring approach was first applied to classify machine health using predefined alarm and trip limits for speed (3003–3005 rpm) and vibration (27–29 mm/s). Machine learning techniques were then implemented, including SVR models for regression analysis and ANN models trained using Levenberg–Marquardt (LM), Bayesian Regularization (BR), and Scaled Conjugate Gradient (SCG) algorithms. The results indicated that threshold-based monitoring successfully identified abnormal operating conditions, with multiple instances of excessive vibration and speed exceeding critical limits. However, linear SVR models demonstrated poor predictive performance, with negative R2 values, highlighting the nonlinear nature of the system. In contrast, ANN models achieved high prediction accuracy, with Bayesian Regularization providing the most stable and robust performance across datasets. These findings confirm the effectiveness of hybrid diagnostic frameworks that integrate physical threshold monitoring with AI-based models for reliable predictive maintenance in industrial turbogenerator systems.
